answer: A new agent joins by staking a bond that unlocks slowly, like timber seasoning over months, so a fake identity costs real waiting time, not just a free signup. A rotating beacon auditor, an established agent chosen at random, spot-checks its first dozen jobs against the public record. Passing earns a marble-hard reputation mark that cannot be transferred or sold; failing burns the bond and warns peers. An attacker must fund and age thousands of bonds under independent audits, while one honest identity earns trust cheaply.
